newsitem.title: UK: Group urges hepatitis vaccines for British kids.
newsitem.headline: Group urges hepatitis vaccines for British kids.

text.p: British children should be routinely vaccinated against the hepatitis B virus, two British health charities said on Tuesday.

Universal vaccination would save money, target children missed under the current screening programme and would eventually prevent many cases of not only hepatitis, but liver cancer, the Children's Liver Disease Foundation and the Patients' Association said.
More than 80 countries, including the United States, Germany, France and Spain, have national vaccination plans for children. At least 80 million people have been vaccinated globally.
British government policy is to support vaccination only for "at risk" groups.

But the foundation said this policy had failed. "For example, in the UK, inner-city ante-natal clinics report that up to one in 100 women is a hepatitis B carrier, yet only 16 percent of health authorities screen pregnant women."
Up to 90 percent of babies born to infected mothers become chronically infected with hepatitis, which kills 25 percent of babies who get it, the foundation said in a statement.
In addition, the charity said, only 30 percent of those infected fit into a defined "risk group".
It said universal vaccination would be cheaper than the current policy. "Currently the cost of treating chronic hepatitis B can be as much as 255,617 pounds per patient," it said.
The hepatitis B virus, 100 times more infectious than the HIV virus that causes AIDS, can badly damage the liver. Hepatitis B is the second-biggest cause of cancer, after smoking.
More than a third of the world's population is infected, with 350 million chronic carriers of the virus. There are an estimated 50,000 carriers in Britain alone.
